chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ سَمَاعَةُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْخُذُهُ الْمُشْرِكُونَ فَتَحْضُرُهُ الصَّلَاةُ فَيَخَافُ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يَمْنَعُوهُ

translations.en: about a man whom the polytheists capture, then the time of salat comes upon him, and he fears that they will prevent him.

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who is unable to perform salat normally because of fear and coercion. It indicates that when outward performance is prevented by hostile captors, salat is still observed through gesturing.
en.seo_question: How should a captive who fears being prevented from praying perform salat?

key_terms.الْمُشْرِكُونَ: the polytheists who have captured the man
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat whose time has arrived
key_terms.يَمْنَعُوهُ: that they may stop him from performing salat
key_terms.يُومِئُ: he performs by making a gesture
key_terms.إِيمَاءً: a physical indication or gesture in place of full movements
